sources.ref_file_title: CHKV25 - Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption from Linear Homomorphism and Sparse LPN
sources.authors: Henry Corrigan-Gibbs, Alexandra Henzinger, Yael Tauman Kalai, Vinod Vaikuntanathan
sources.note: Bibliographic data verified against vendor/cryptobib (EC:CHKV25, doi 10.1007/978-3-031-91124-8_1; EPRINT:CHKV24 = 2024/1760). Abstract names DDH and DCR as instantiations of the linearly homomorphic component.

pages.class_justification: CHKV25 make no RTV-style claim. The construction uses the linearly homomorphic PKE generically, but the sparse-LPN component is a concrete algebraic scheme and the edge mixes an assumption with a primitive; recording a class the source does not state would add a claim.
pages.statement: [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]] and [[learning-parity-with-noise#sparse-learning-parity-with-noise|sparse LPN]] together yield [[homomorphic-encryption#somewhat-homomorphic-encryption-she|somewhat homomorphic encryption]]: sparse LPN plus any [[homomorphic-encryption#partially-homomorphic-encryption-phe|linearly homomorphic PKE]] gives SHE, and DDH instantiates the linearly homomorphic component. The scheme supports $O(\log \secpar / \log \log \secpar)$ homomorphic multiplications followed by $\poly(\secpar)$ additions, and evaluated ciphertexts have bit-length a fixed polynomial in $\secpar$, independent of the number of operations applied — [[CHKV25 - Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption from Linear Homomorphism and Sparse LPN|CHKV25]].

CHKV25's abstract states the DDH instantiation explicitly, so the edge is citable as-is; a human should decide whether the wiki keeps both the generic edge and its DDH/DCR instantiations.
The conjunctive structure (both hypotheses needed) is correct as recorded.

sources.ref_file_title: DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications
sources.authors: Nico Döttling, Sanjam Garg, Yuval Ishai, Giulio Malavolta, Tamer Mour, Rafail Ostrovsky
sources.note: Bibliographic data verified against vendor/cryptobib (C:DGIMMO19, doi 10.1007/978-3-030-26954-8_1; EPRINT:DGIMMO19 = 2019/639). Abstract: TDH with one-bit hints from DDH, QR, DCR, or LWE.

pages.class_justification: DGI+19 do not classify the reduction; the construction is a concrete group-based scheme from an assumption, so the RTV primitive-from-primitive taxonomy is not stated by the source.
pages.model_justification: The DDH-based construction is in the standard model (no idealized oracle).
pages.statement: [[decisional-diffie-hellman|DDH]] implies [[trapdoor-hash-function|trapdoor hash functions]] for the index predicates $f_i(x) = x_i$ with one-bit hints; the same framework instantiates from QR, DCR, and LWE — [[DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications|DGI+19]].
pages.sketch: The hash key is a $2 \times n$ matrix of group elements $(g_{j,b})$ and $H(x) = \prod_j g_{j,x_j}$. The encoding key for index $i$ raises every entry to a secret exponent $s$ and additionally multiplies the $(i,1)$ entry by $g$, so evaluating on $x$ gives $H(x)^s \cdot g^{x_i}$; the trapdoor $s$ recovers $x_i$ from $H(x)$, a distributed discrete-logarithm step compresses the hint to a single bit, and DDH makes the perturbed entry indistinguishable from the others, hiding $i$.
notes_to_keep: DGI+19's DDH-based TDH has its own rate/parameter constraints (one-bit hints, rate-1 variants, correctness error) that the edge cannot carry; they are load-bearing for the downstream polylog-communication PIR claim on tdh-to-cpir-amr25.
flags: COMPOSITE chain correctly split by migration: DDH => TDH (this page) and TDH => PIR (tdh-to-cpir-amr25) are separate links, both in DGI+19.

Sketch verified from verifier knowledge of the DGI+19 DDH construction only (eprint unreachable this session); the perturbed-entry/subset-product mechanism is standard, but a human with the paper should confirm the one-bit-hint step wording before status goes beyond draft.
verifier_changes: statement: removed the downstream PIR sentence (that is the separate edge tdh-to-cpir-amr25) and led with DDH => TDH
sketch: 'i-th column perturbed' -> the (i,1) entry multiplied by g, made E(ek,x) = H(x)^s g^{x_i} explicit, and named the distributed discrete-log compression that yields the one-bit hint
confidence high -> medium: sketch could not be checked against the paper text this session

pages.class_justification: The construction is the identity (the LWE instance is unchanged) and the reduction is one fixed algorithm that runs any search-LWE solver once as an oracle and post-processes its output with a residual check. This is the RTV04 fully-black-box shape, degenerately instantiated for an assumption-to-assumption edge; it holds for parameters where the residual check is meaningful (efficiently recognizable error distribution, m large enough that uniform u is far from every As).
pages.statement: If [[learning-with-errors#decision-lwe|decision LWE]] is hard for $(n, q, \chi, m)$ then [[learning-with-errors#search-lwe|search LWE]] is hard for the same parameters, provided $\chi$ is efficiently recognizable (e.g. bounded) and $m$ is large enough that a uniform $\mathbf{u} \in \ZZ_q^m$ lies within error distance of some $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{s}$ only with negligible probability: a search solver yields a decision distinguisher with the same advantage up to a negligible term — folklore.
pages.sketch: Given $(\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{u})$, run the search solver to obtain $\hat{\mathbf{s}}$ and output "LWE" iff $\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{A}\hat{\mathbf{s}}$ lies in the support of $\chi^m$. On LWE samples the check passes whenever the solver succeeds; on uniform samples no candidate secret passes except with negligible probability.
flags: HIGH PRIORITY - SWAPPED BODIES: the migrated quote on this page describes the coordinate-by-coordinate reduction that uses a DECISION oracle to solve SEARCH. Under the repo's hardness-implication convention that reduction proves search-hard => decision-hard, i.e. it belongs on the converse page search-lwe-to-decision-lwe (batch red-29), whose own migrated quote (solve-and-check) in turn belongs here. The two pages' Statement quotes must be exchanged; coordinate with red-29.

The displaced coordinate-recovery reduction is due to Reg05 and requires prime q = poly(n); its O(q n m) sample count and the modulus restriction should travel with it to search-lwe-to-decision-lwe, which should become disposition sourced (Reg05) rather than folklore.

The parameter conditions (recognizable chi, m large enough) are now stated in the statement; for m <= n the check is vacuous, but search LWE is then information-theoretically hard, so the implication is not falsified.
verifier_changes: statement: added the load-bearing parameter conditions (recognizable error distribution, m large enough) instead of an unqualified 'same parameters'; 'essentially the same advantage' -> 'same advantage up to a negligible term'
sketch: 'plausible error vector' -> 'lies in the support of chi^m'; removed the vague 'for m sufficiently larger than n' (now in the statement)
class_justification: scoped the fully-black-box claim to the parameter regime where the residual check works

pages.wrong_reason: Misattribution, as the page's own SUSPECT note says. KSW08's inner-product predicate encryption scheme is not proven secure under DLIN: it lives in a composite-order bilinear group of order N = pqr and its (selective) attribute-hiding proof rests on two new subgroup-decision-flavoured assumptions that KSW08 justify only in the generic bilinear group model; DLIN appears nowhere as the hypothesis. The wiki's own KSW08 reference page carries a fabricated abstract sentence ('proved secure in the standard model under the decisional linear assumption') that likely seeded the error. 'DLIN implies attribute-hiding IPPE' is true but belongs to other papers: adaptively secure, fully attribute-hiding inner-product encryption under DLIN is Okamoto-Takashima, 'Adaptively Attribute-Hiding (Hierarchical) Inner Product Encryption', EUROCRYPT 2012 (cryptobib EC:OkaTak12, eprint 2011/543); Freeman's prime-order conversion of KSW08 (EUROCRYPT 2010, cryptobib EC:Freeman10) is the likely source of a DLIN-based selectively secure variant, to be checked against that paper. Correct repair: either re-source this edge as KSW08's actual theorem (composite-order subgroup-decision assumptions => selectively attribute-hiding IPPE) or retitle it dlin-to-ippe-ot12 with OT12 as source; fix the source bullet on inner-product-predicate-encryption.md and the KSW08 reference page in the same pass.
flags: The migration's SUSPECT note is confirmed: KSW08 uses two new assumptions in composite-order (N = pqr) bilinear groups, proven only in the generic group model, not DLIN.

pages.class_justification: Identity construction: the PIR protocol runs the DEPIR algorithms unchanged (the server runs Setup on its own database, the client runs Qry/Fin), and any PIR privacy adversary is verbatim a DEPIR privacy adversary. Both the construction and the reduction use their objects only as oracles. Scoped to the unkeyed (default) and public-key variants; see flags.
pages.statement: An unkeyed [[doubly-efficient-pir|DEPIR]] scheme is a [[single-server-private-information-retrieval|single-server PIR]] whose database is preprocessed: the server runs $\Setup(1^\secpar, DB)$ itself, and the query phase is a two-message PIR with query-time communication and computation $o(n)$; correctness and query privacy carry over unchanged. A public-key DEPIR is likewise a PIR once the server publishes $k$, since privacy holds given $k$; a secret-key DEPIR is not, since its privacy requires $k$ hidden from the server — folklore.
notes_to_keep: Definitional specialization ('is a type of'), not a theorem with a proof in some paper; the folklore label is the citation.
flags: SCOPE CAVEAT: the implication is definitional only for unkeyed DEPIR (the page's default) and for PK-DEPIR with k published. For SK-DEPIR it fails: privacy holds only against adversaries not given k, so a server that runs Setup itself gets no guarantee, and a client cannot preprocess a database it does not hold. The statement now says this; consider narrowing the hypothesis to [[doubly-efficient-pir#unkeyed-depir|unkeyed DEPIR]].
The migration note 'implication direction is DEPIR => single-server PIR, opposite to the surface word order' is resolved: the recorded orientation (hypotheses: depir, conclusion: cpir) is correct.
verifier_changes: statement: moved the SK-DEPIR exclusion and the PK-DEPIR condition into the statement itself so the page does not assert an unqualified DEPIR => PIR
class_justification: scoped to unkeyed/public-key variants

sources.ref_file_title: GGHW14 - On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input
sources.authors: Sanjam Garg, Craig Gentry, Shai Halevi, Daniel Wichs
sources.note: Bibliographic data verified against vendor/cryptobib (C:GGHW14, doi 10.1007/978-3-662-44371-2_29; EPRINT:GGHW13 = 2013/860). Evidence that general-purpose diO with arbitrary auxiliary input does not exist, so the blanket equivalence with iO is implausible.

pages.class_justification: Identity construction: the diO obfuscator is used unchanged as the iO obfuscator. The reduction is fixed: an iO distinguisher for a functionally equivalent pair is directly a diO adversary for the constant sampler outputting that pair, which is unconditionally differing-inputs-hard because no differing input exists.
pages.statement: A [[indistinguishability-obfuscation#differing-inputs-obfuscation-dio|differing-inputs obfuscator]] for a circuit class is an [[indistinguishability-obfuscation|indistinguishability obfuscator]] for the same class: functionally equivalent circuits admit no differing input, so the constant sampler outputting such a pair is differing-inputs-hard and the diO guarantee applies to it — folklore.
pages.improvements_text:
- The converse holds only in restricted form: [[indistinguishability-obfuscation|iO]] for a class implies diO for pairs of circuits in the class that differ on at most polynomially many inputs — [[BCP14 - On Extractability Obfuscation|BCP14]]
- Assuming a special-purpose obfuscator for a specific circuit family, general-purpose diO with arbitrary auxiliary input does not exist — [[GGHW14 - On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input|GGHW14]]
flags: HIGH PRIORITY - KIND: the recorded kind: equivalence is unsupported. Blanket diO <=> iO is neither proven nor believed: the converse (iO => diO) is known only for circuits differing on at most polynomially many inputs (BCP14), and general diO with auxiliary input is implausible (GGHW14). Set kind to implication (diO => iO, matching the frontmatter orientation) and retitle the page; the vague migrated sentence 'equivalent under certain conditions' refers to the BCP14 restricted case, now recorded in improvements.
The trivial direction assumes the standard diO definition quantifying over all (non-uniform) differing-inputs samplers, so constant samplers outputting an equivalent pair are admissible.
If an io-to-dio page restricted to polynomially many differing inputs is ever wanted, it is a separate BCP14-sourced edge, not this one.

Content of BCP14 (iO => eO for polynomially many differing inputs, via binary search over threshold hybrids) and GGHW14 (special-purpose-obfuscation-based implausibility) stated from verifier knowledge; web unreachable this session.

sources.ref_file_title: FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications
sources.authors: Georg Fuchsbauer, Eike Kiltz, Julian Loss
sources.note: Bibliographic data verified against vendor/cryptobib (C:FucKilLos18, doi 10.1007/978-3-319-96881-0_2; eprint 2017/620). Abstract: tight security reduction for BLS to DLOG in the AGM.

pages.class_justification: An AGM reduction reads the algebraic representations the adversary outputs, so it is not black-box in the RTV sense, and FKL18 make no RTV-style classification; the model axis (algebraic-group) carries the restriction.
pages.model_justification: FKL18's BLS analysis is in the AGM combined with the random-oracle model (BLS hashes messages into the group; H is modeled as a programmable random oracle). The model field carries one value; algebraic-group is recorded and the ROM component is stated in the statement text.
pages.statement: In the [[algebraic-group-model|algebraic group model]], with the hash-to-group function modeled as a random oracle, EUF-CMA security of [[digital-signature#bls-signatures|BLS signatures]] reduces tightly to [[discrete-logarithm|DLOG]]: an algebraic forger yields a DLOG solver with essentially the same running time and advantage up to a constant factor — [[FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications|FKL18]].
notes_to_keep: The reduction holds only for algebraic adversaries (AGM) and additionally uses the ROM; outside the AGM, BLS is proven only from CDH in the ROM, with a non-tight reduction, and no DLOG-based proof is known.
flags: CONCLUSION ID: the researcher flagged boneh-lynn-shacham-signature as broken, but digital-signature.md declares it under variants (boneh-lynn-shacham-signature: '#bls-signatures'), so the id resolves; the only broken link is the migrated quote's [[boneh-lynn-shacham-signature|BLS]] wikilink, which should become [[digital-signature#bls-signatures|BLS]].

MODEL: the single-valued model field cannot express AGM+ROM. The repo elsewhere encodes ROM as an explicit hypothesis object (cf. dlog-and-rom-to-schnorr-signatures-sch91); either add rom as a hypothesis or keep model algebraic-group with the ROM stated in the page body, but be consistent across the FKL18 edges.

sources.ref_file_title: FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications
sources.authors: Georg Fuchsbauer, Eike Kiltz, Julian Loss
sources.note: Bibliographic data verified against vendor/cryptobib (C:FucKilLos18, doi 10.1007/978-3-319-96881-0_2; eprint 2017/620). Abstract: CDH (among other assumptions) shown equivalent to DLOG in the AGM.

pages.class_justification: The reduction extracts from the algebraic representation the AGM obliges the adversary to output, so it is not black-box in the RTV sense and FKL18 make no RTV-style classification; the model axis carries the restriction.
pages.model_justification: Load-bearing: the reduction works only for algebraic adversaries; no standard-model reduction from DLOG hardness to CDH hardness is known.
pages.statement: In the [[algebraic-group-model|algebraic group model]], [[computational-diffie-hellman|CDH]] is as hard as [[discrete-logarithm|DLOG]]: an algebraic CDH adversary converts into a DLOG solver with the same advantage and essentially the same running time, so DLOG hardness implies CDH hardness for algebraic adversaries — [[FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications|FKL18]].
pages.sketch: The reduction rerandomizes a DLOG challenge $Z = g^z$ in a prime-order group into a CDH instance $(X, Y)$ whose exponents are known affine functions of $z$. The adversary returns its answer with coefficients expressing it as a product of powers of $g$, $X$, and $Y$; a correct answer then satisfies a quadratic equation in $z$ over $\ZZ_p$ with nonzero leading coefficient, whose at most two roots the reduction computes and checks against $Z$.
pages.security_loss: tight: same advantage and essentially the same running time (FKL18)
notes_to_keep: MODEL IS LOAD-BEARING: the reduction holds only for algebraic adversaries; dropping model: algebraic-group would turn a model-relative reduction into a standard-model implication that is not known.
flags: The page's second migrated quote (composing 'these reductions' with the Sho97 generic-group lower bound to get concrete bounds against 'algebraic-and-generic adversaries') is a separate lower-bound statement, not part of this edge; per the migration REPAIR PATCH note it should move to a barrier/lower-bound record, and its AGM-to-GGM transfer step is contested by KZ22 (cf. barrier no-agm-to-ggm-kz22).

FKL18 state an equivalence (CDH =_AGM DLOG); the converse hardness direction (CDH hard => DLOG hard) is the trivial standard-model edge and exists as the separate page cdh-to-dlog, so kind stays implication on both.

Sketch mechanism (rerandomization, representation gives a quadratic in z, root-finding) is from verifier knowledge; the exact rerandomization the paper uses could not be checked this session, so the sketch states it generically.
verifier_changes: sketch: replaced the specific embedding (W g^r, W g^s) with the generic 'exponents are known affine functions of z' so the sketch is correct whichever rerandomization FKL18 use; 'monic quadratic' -> 'quadratic with nonzero leading coefficient'
model_justification: dropped 'as the migration note says'
flags: recorded that the sketch could not be compared with the paper text

pages.class_justification: Membership of a problem in a complexity class is proved by any argument at all; free is the repo convention for proven complexity containments.
pages.statement: The decision version of [[discrete-logarithm|DLOG]] — given $(\GG, g, p, X, t)$, decide whether the $x \in [p]$ with $g^x = X$ satisfies $x \le t$ — is in [[co-nondeterministic-polynomial-time|coNP]]: a no-instance is certified by $x$ itself, since $g^x = X$ and $x > t$ are checkable in polynomial time and $x$ is unique once the order $p$ of $g$ is certified by its prime factorization with primality certificates — folklore.
notes_to_keep: `class: free` because a containment between complexity classes is proved by any argument at all; the reduction-class axis does not discriminate here.
flags: The migrated quote states DLOG in NP intersect coNP; this page records the coNP half and the companion dlog-to-np (batch red-08) records the NP half — the statements should mirror each other.
Stale boilerplate: the Notes still carry the '`class: unstated`' explanation although the frontmatter already says class: free; drop it.

DLOG is a search/promise problem; the containment is about its natural decision version (threshold on the exponent), which the statement makes explicit. The certificate needs the order of g to be verifiable (Pratt-style primality certificates in concrete groups); with the wiki's GrGen promise the order p is given.
verifier_changes: statement: tightened — merged the two certificate clauses into one sentence and made explicit that the no-certificate is x with g^x = X and x > t, unique given a certified order
